Keybinding.networkRemoveHint: With a creature in focus, takes off the line or symbol the pointer is on (or Tab stepped to).
Keybinding.networkLowerHint: With a creature in focus, lowers the line or symbol the pointer is on (or Tab stepped to); at its least, takes it off.
Keybinding.networkRaiseHint: With a creature in focus, raises the line or symbol the pointer is on (or Tab stepped to). On the creature itself, adds a line from it.
Keybinding.networkNextHint: Steps to the next of the focused creature's lines and symbols (with nobody in focus, the next creature).
Keybinding.networkPreviousHint: Steps back to the last of the focused creature's lines and symbols (with nobody in focus, the creature before).

Generic.Label: Generic d20 (configured paths)
Generic.MenuHint: For game systems without a FastFighting helper module: where to find HP, AC, attack bonus and damage on actors.
Generic.Hint: Property paths on the actor, e.g. system.attributes.hp.value. Leave attack or damage empty to estimate them from level.

Path.perception: Perception modifier (optional; the initiative stands in without it)

predictionTime.Name: Prediction time (seconds)
predictionTime.Hint: How long the planner's prediction runs: fight after fight until the time is up (the one under way is finished). More time, more fights and surer odds. A big battle gets fewer fights in the same time, since every creature adds to each fight's work. The planner can change it for one battle.

maxRounds.Name: Max rounds
maxRounds.Hint: A simulated battle still going after this many rounds counts as a stalemate.

includeHidden.Name: Include hidden tokens
includeHidden.Hint: Hidden tokens (ambushers, reinforcements) take part in estimates by default.

includeOtherLevels.Name: Include other scene levels
includeOtherLevels.Hint: Include tokens on scene Levels other than the one being viewed.

neutralDefault.Name: Neutral tokens
neutralDefault.Hint: Default handling of tokens with Neutral disposition. They stand on the field taking no side, perhaps leaning one way: whoever hurts or robs them, or crosses what they want (hurting someone they lean toward), turns them against their side, and either side's talkers can try to win them over (harder against their lean). Can be changed per battle and per token.

downedModel.Name: Downed characters
downedModel.Hint: How falling to 0 HP is simulated. 'Simulate dying and healing' follows the system's rules for dying, recovery and revival.

pcHealAggro.Name: Default PC healing
pcHealAggro.Hint: How freely player characters spend spells, potions and actions on healing, unless set per character. "Let each character decide" leaves it to each one: its class, its features and its nature.

pcAllyDying.Name: Default PC response to a dying ally
pcAllyDying.Hint: What player characters prioritize when an ally is dying, unless set per character. "Let each character decide" leaves it to each one: its class, its features and its nature.

leadership.Name: Leadership
leadership.Hint: Leaders (best social or warfare skill, Commanders, rallying abilities) raise their side's bravery and coordination while standing.

morale.Name: Morale and routing
morale.Hint: Combatants may waver or flee based on bravery, wounds, losses and a fallen leader or master.

positioning.Name: Positioning and terrain
positioning.Hint: Use token distances, movement types, terrain costs, walls and elevation. Turn off for theater-of-the-mind scenes.

surpriseDefault.Name: Initiative
surpriseDefault.Hint: Use the combat tracker's initiative when present, roll Stealth for hidden or Secret tokens, or roll normally.

lootMode.Name: Do it For Real Now: loot
lootMode.Hint: What happens to a slain creature's gear: leave it on the corpse (lootable), drop it in a loot pile, or do nothing.

corpseMode.Name: Do it For Real Now: corpses
corpseMode.Hint: Keep slain tokens on the map with the dead marker, or remove them (when a loot pile is dropped).

fledMode.Name: Do it For Real Now: fled combatants
fledMode.Hint: Hide tokens that fled the battle, or leave them where they are.

sideDefaults.Name: Side personality defaults
sideDefaults.Label: Configure
sideDefaults.Hint: Default group Tactical, Brave, Selfish and Loyal values for Friendly, Hostile, Neutral and Secret sides.

talking.Name: Talking
talking.Hint: Characters may try to de-escalate: talk enemies who share a language into surrendering, fleeing, giving something up or (rarely, unless they came as neutrals) standing aside; and talk those who take no side into joining them, or leaving.

ignoreLanguages.Name: Ignore languages
ignoreLanguages.Hint: Anyone who speaks at least one language understands anyone else who does, so talking never fails for want of a shared language. Creatures with no language at all (beasts, the mindless) still can't be talked to. Can be changed per battle.

storyStyle.Name: Story style
storyStyle.Hint: How the story of a fight is told in the Sample fight tab and in the chat by Do it For Real Now: Roleplay (prose), Standard (what everyone did) or Statistician (every roll, for the GMs).

storyMode.Name: Story delivery
storyMode.Hint: Post the story publicly, or whisper it to GMs only.

bystanders.Name: Bystanders can join
bystanders.Hint: Tokens on the map that are not in the encounter may notice the fight (by sight or sound, muffled by walls), be called for help, be hunted, or be run into by someone fleeing, and then decide whether to join.

genericFallback.Name: Use the experimental generic adapter
genericFallback.Hint: Only for systems without a FastFighting helper module: guess HP, AC, attacks and damage from configured data paths. Expect rough results.

aftermath.Name: After the fight
aftermath.Hint: Survivors tend the dying (and the story tells it), the story ends at the last blow, or everyone stays as the fight left them.

opening.Name: How encounters open
opening.Hint: Talk if they'd rather (a standoff when the leaders would rather talk), always talk first, straight to battle, or only an argument (never comes to blows).

concedeLuck.Name: PC luck: handing over an item
concedeLuck.Hint: When a player character is talked into giving up an item, they lose it only if a hidden d100 comes up at or under this. Higher means PCs lose items more often.

theftLuck.Name: PC luck: being robbed
theftLuck.Hint: A thief who beats a player character's defenses still needs a hidden d100 at or under this to take anything. Higher means thieves succeed more often.

playOnMap.Name: Do it For Real Now: play the fight on the map
playOnMap.Hint: Each turn's tokens move as its card is posted. Off: they go straight to where the fight leaves them.

storyOdds.Name: Show the odds in the posted story
storyOdds.Hint: Adds each side's chance of winning, as the simulation saw it, to the end of the story. The planner has the same switch.

standGround.Name: Doesn't like to flee: how often it stays (%)
standGround.Hint: A character whose answer to when to retreat is Fight to the end ignores the urge to run away this often (half as often for When the battle turns against us), when running is its own choice (shaken nerve, a terror close by, a planned retreat); talked out of the fight, it gives up where it stands instead of running just as often. Fear a spell or the rules put on it still works as the system says.

avoidKilling.Name: Avoids killing: how often it holds back (%)
avoidKilling.Hint: A character whose answer to who it attacks first is "I avoid killing" holds back this often (50 to 90, default 90; less for answers that lean less that way): a blow that would kill knocks out instead, it leaves the fallen be, and after the fight it spares them. Nobody controls the story entirely: now and then it kills all the same.

neutralReach.Name: Neutral friend groups: reach (squares)
neutralReach.Hint: When the Battle Planner opens, it proposes friend groups for the neutral tokens: from the map's top-left corner, the nearest neutral starts group 1 with every neutral of its kind; anyone within this many squares of the group joins it, and so on, up to three steps out. Group 2 starts the same way; everyone left is group 3. The GM can move anyone with the 1 2 3 pills.

switchLuck.Name: Luck: an enemy changing sides
switchLuck.Hint: When an enemy is talked into changing sides, it goes through with it only if a hidden d100 comes up under this; otherwise it's talked into something else (surrendering, standing down, running). Even then it only stands aside, taking no side, and has to be won over from there. 100 means it always does. Doesn't touch spells and abilities made for it (charm, dominate), or talking round someone who already takes no side.

executeLuck.Name: PC luck: being finished off
executeLuck.Hint: Each time a creature wants to kill a player character who's down at 0 HP, it goes ahead only if a hidden d100 comes up at or under this; otherwise it turns away to its next foe, taking everything it wanted of that PC along. Higher means fallen PCs die more often.

leaderInfluence.Name: Leader's influence
leaderInfluence.Hint: How readily followers take their lead outright from whoever commands their group, on a scale of 0 to 100 (50 is the usual; it isn't a percentage). A leader always counts a little: its wishes pull on its followers every turn. On top of that, each turn a follower may follow outright, as its loyalty and playstyles allow: it then takes up what its commander wants most (that it can actually do) in proportion to how strongly the commander wants it, and its playstyle leans toward its commander's for the turn. 0: nobody follows outright; 100: twice as readily as usual.

bossInfluence.Name: Boss's influence
bossInfluence.Hint: How much more readily followers take a boss's lead than a leader's: 1.25 to 3 times (default 2). A group with a boss has no leader; a lieutenant who steps up for a fallen boss leads as a leader, never as a boss. The party never has a boss.

traitorLuck.Name: Luck check: a player character turning traitor
traitorLuck.Hint: A player character who wants to lead, isn't its group's leader, and is scheming against whoever is (a playstyle like Cruel or Wildcard with Wants to Lead) can be talked into changing sides only on a d100 roll of this or less (default 9). 0: never.

trapLuck.Name: Trap avoiders: spotting a trap (%)
trapLuck.Hint: A trap avoider (a character whose playstyles keep it watchful: Thief most, then Puzzle-Maniac, Skeptic, Lore-Collector, Chicken and Wallflower) spots each hazard only if a hidden d100 comes up at or under this (default 59) times how watchful it is: all of it for a Thief, about a third for a Wallflower, less for a pill further down. It then keeps out of that hazard's reach as it moves, going around it, and goes in only for something it wants badly enough. Anyone a hazard goes for knows it from then on. 0: never; 100: always.

tauntLuck.Name: Playstyle taunts: taking hold (%)
tauntLuck.Hint: A character whose playstyles make it a taunter (Tank most, then Instigator, Martyr, Brawler and Redeem-Seeker) may spend an action goading a foe into coming at it: its talking (threats or mockery) against the foe's resistance, then, if that gets through, a hidden d100 at or under this (default 42) times how much of a taunter it is (all of it for a Tank as its first pick; less for the others, and for a pill further down). Taken hold, the foe wants to go for it until the end of its next turn. Only playstyle taunts use this: a game system's taunts (skills, powers, spells) follow their own rules. 0: never; 100: always, when the talking works.

partySway.Name: Party's sway (%)
partySway.Hint: How much the player party's wishes (the players' votes in the survey's Party tab, majority rules) sway everyone on the friendly side: in that share of fights a character uses the party's answer where it left its own to "Let this character decide", and the party's wishes add that much to what each wants (on the 0 to 100 desire scale).

playersRunPCs.Name: Players run their characters
playersRunPCs.Hint: Do it For Real Now plays the battle on the combat tracker: players take their own turns, FastFighting plays everyone else. Off: FastFighting plays every turn. Each battle can say otherwise.

ignoreTroubles.Name: Selfless creatures bear what holds or hurts them (%)
ignoreTroubles.Hint: Each turn a creature held fast, prone, or hurting (on fire, bleeding) would try to be rid of it as much as it bothers it. A fully selfless one that doesn't stop to calculate bears it instead, on a hidden d100 at or under this (default 29), and keeps at what it wants; the more self-serving or calculating it is, the smaller its share of this. Never what would kill it. 0: nobody bears it; 100: the selfless always do.

preferredAction.Label: Favorite weapon or attack
preferredAction.Hint: Its go-to attack; it still switches when something else is clearly better.

style.Label: Fighting style
style.frontline: Front line: close in and hold the line
style.skirmisher: Skirmisher: flank, strike twice, keep moving
style.ranged: Ranged: keep my distance and shoot
style.protector: Protector: guard my allies, shield up

target.Label: Who to pursue first
target.Hint: Who it goes after first: to fight, or to talk round.

fallen.Label: Foes who fall
fallen.Hint: What it does with a foe who's down. Spare them: never a killing blow, and first aid after. Tie them up: taken alive (mostly no killing blow), a prisoner even if healed.

resourceUse.Label: Spell slots, focus and limited abilities
resourceUse.Hint: How readily it spends what only comes back after rest.
resourceUse.balanced: Use them when they are clearly better
resourceUse.nova: Spend freely to end it fast

specialty.Label: Magic and specialties
specialty.Hint: How often it uses its spells and special abilities over a plain weapon, moves or talk.

consumables.Label: Consumables
consumables.Hint: How readily it uses up potions, scrolls and bombs. Anyone will to save a life.
consumables.avoid: I don't like to use consumables
consumables.freely: Consumables are here to get used

healAggro.Label: Healing others
healAggro.Hint: How freely it spends actions and resources healing allies.
healAggro.conservative: Only when someone is dying or badly hurt
healAggro.allCosts: Heal at all costs, even with my last resources

allyDying.Label: When an ally is dying
allyDying.Hint: What it does when a friend goes down.

selfRevived.Label: After I'm revived
selfRevived.Hint: What it does after getting back up.

retreat.Label: When to retreat
retreat.losing: When the battle turns against us

shield.Label: Shield or defending
shield.Hint: How it uses Raise a Shield or a defensive turn (Dodge).
shield.spare: With spare actions, or when it's worth it

talk.Label: Talking instead of fighting
talk.Hint: Tries to end fights with words: persuade, threaten or bluff foes who share a language.
talk.always: Always talk unless I am currently being hurt
talk.first: Talk first: try to end it with words
talk.never: Let my weapons do the talking

beyond.Label: Others nearby
beyond.Hint: Creatures on the map not in the encounter: run to them for help, or hunt them after winning.
beyond.seekHelp: Run for help when it goes badly

Playstyle.Label: Playstyles
Playstyle.Hint: Up to 4, most important first; later ones count less. They shape "Let this character decide".
Playstyle.Max: Pick at most four playstyles. Unpick one first.
Playstyle.StayTrue: Stay mostly true to my calculated tactical level

chicken.Name: Chicken
chicken.Hint: Much less brave: hangs back, drinks potions early, flees when hurt. Avoids the most dangerous foe.

cruel.Name: Cruel
cruel.Hint: Picks on the weakest, finishes the fallen, hits back hard.

moralist.Name: Moralist
moralist.Hint: Never strikes a fallen foe; heals friends, guards the weakest, calms quarrels.

peacekeeper.Name: Peacekeeper
peacekeeper.Hint: Keeps the peace: calms quarrels, talks foes into standing down, never threatens, spares the fallen.

peoplePleaser.Name: People-Pleaser
peoplePleaser.Hint: Goes along with the group: follows its leader, heals freely, protects friends, talks fighters out of fighting.

fragile.Name: Fragile
fragile.Hint: Drinks potions early and flees when hurt; once hurt, wants to get away and mend.

impatient.Name: Impatient
impatient.Hint: Charges the nearest foe, spends freely, skips the shield. Short fuse.

brawler.Name: Brawler
brawler.Hint: Loves melee: front line, nearest foe, hits back hard, no talking.

skeptic.Name: Skeptic
skeptic.Hint: Careful: saves resources, heals sparingly, hard to talk round, half swayed by its leader. Sees through taunts.

speedRunner.Name: Speed-Runner
speedRunner.Hint: Wants it over fast: spends everything, quickest kills first.

leader.Name: Wants to Lead
leader.Hint: Wants to lead: braver, loyal, goes for the biggest threat, rallies its people. Half ignores other commanders.

instigator.Name: Instigator
instigator.Hint: Acts first: locks foes down, picks fights with the most dangerous foe and their leader. Taunts foes.

diplomat.Name: Diplomat
diplomat.Hint: Talks first and throughout, calms quarrels, often spares the fallen. Cool-headed when taunted.

wallflower.Name: Wallflower
wallflower.Hint: Stays at range and out of notice; would rather hamper than hit. Often ignores taunts.

martyr.Name: Martyr
martyr.Hint: Never retreats, heals at all costs, guards the weakest, avenges the fallen. Taunts foes off friends.

tank.Name: Tank
tank.Hint: Takes the blows: taunts foes off friends, guards the weakest, never retreats, shield up.

mercenary.Name: Mercenary
mercenary.Hint: In it for itself: easy targets, saves resources, little loyalty, gives up when it gets hard.

enabler.Name: Enabler
enabler.Hint: Support first: heals, guards and bolsters friends; backs the leader.

redeemSeeker.Name: Redeem-Seeker
redeemSeeker.Hint: Out to prove itself: takes on the biggest threat from the front line, never gives up.

loreCollector.Name: Lore-Collector
loreCollector.Hint: Sizes up new foes first, then rolls much better against their kind; may share what it learns.

puzzleManiac.Name: Puzzle-Maniac
puzzleManiac.Hint: Very tactical: exploits weaknesses, targets casters, loves lock-downs and locked doors.

wildcard.Name: Wildcard
wildcard.Hint: Unpredictable: random targets, ignores advice, may defy its leader.

thief.Name: Thief
thief.Hint: Light fingers: may rob a foe within reach when winning or unseen. A lock is an invitation.

Playstyle.AvoidCostlySpells: I don't like to use spells that cost something
Playstyle.AvoidCostlySpellsHint: Spells that use slots, focus or daily uses only when a life is at stake. Cantrips are free.

vengeful.Name: Vengeful
vengeful.Hint: Never forgets: hits back twice as hard, avenges fallen friends.

relentless.Name: Relentless
relentless.Hint: Single-minded: sticks with its foe, shrugs off setbacks, hard to taunt away.

lazy.Name: Lazy
lazy.Hint: Does as little as it can: nearest foe, saves resources, gives up fast.

unmundane.Name: Un-Mundane
unmundane.Hint: Leans on its magic and special abilities over plain weapons or talk; spends freely.

Party.Intro: How do you want everyone in the party to act? One vote per player, and only the votes of players logged in count. Majority rules: the most-voted answer to each question is the party's, and it sways everyone on your side a little in every fight. A tie goes to the party's leader; a tie the leader doesn't settle counts as no answer. Vote again to take your vote back; swipe Lock-in when you're done (until your GM sends everyone a new survey). Closing the survey locks your votes too.
Party.GmView: Only the players vote. You see everyone's votes; the outlined answer is the party's.
Party.ReadOnly: The party's wishes, to look at: you can vote on them again when your GM sends everyone the survey.
